_why: REPORT-31 M31-0. Each entry binds a parity oracle to the c43 file whose behaviour it reproduces. `frozen` oracles are hand-transliterated and CANNOT see c43 move, so they are gated on a content hash of what they mirror; the endpoint is an empty list, not a maintained one. `generated` oracles are extracted from c43 source and are sound in shape -- they are gated on reproducing byte-identically, because nothing else re-runs the extractor.
_converted: flags_oracle.c left this list in M31-2 and program_serialization_oracle.c in M31-3: each now #includes its c43 counterpart under oracle_* names, so the reference moves with c43 by construction and there is nothing left to hash. Entries leave here by being converted, never by being excused.

frozen.why: 1060 lines, 43 oracle_* functions -- the largest frozen reference. Reimplements setRegisterDataType, so a widened register tag field changes registers.c, changes nothing here, and the lane agrees with an unported Zig owner. BLOCKED, not infeasible: registers.c compiles clean against upstream's own c47.h (4 placeholder GTK/glib typedefs + the generated constantPointers.h) and needs only ~85 one-line stubs -- but a compiled-from-c43 oracle uses c43's reserved-variable block, and z47 still uses the pre-SPARE model (FIRST_NAMED_RESERVED_VARIABLE 2026 vs c43's 2031). audit-constant-parity.py already reports and allowlists that deferral. Resolve it first, then convert; converting first yields either a permanently red lane or a doctored oracle.

194 lines against saveRestoreCalcState.c's 2959 -- it mirrors save-file revision parsing and nothing else, while the lane is named for the whole subsystem. NEXT TO CONVERT (option A, unblocked): saveRestoreCalcState.c compiles clean against upstream's c47.h with 194 undefined symbols, all one-line stubs. It is also the only lane that could hold z47's .sav FORMAT to c43's -- M31-1 established that saveload_roundtrip's golden is a z47 self-portrait, so nothing detects c43 changing the save format today.

238 lines against keyboard.c's 4982 -- ~4% coverage under a subsystem-wide lane name. NOT to be converted this way: keyboard.c is the one file the compile-from-c43 recipe fails on, because it reads GdkEvent fields and declares GdkEventButton by value, so it needs real gtk+-3.0 headers plus 305 stubs. M31-6 chose option C instead -- a differential through keyboard_entry_harness.c, which already drives btnClicked through a full core that links GTK. Delete this oracle as part of landing that differential, not before.

generated.why: Extracted from src/c47/charString.c by its own script, so the reference moves with c43 -- but the script's header comment claimed 'the harness fails if the committed oracle is stale' and nothing in the tree re-ran it. Sound shape, ungated until now.
